newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish insurer PZU chooses adviser, postpones sale.
newsitem.headline: Polish insurer PZU chooses adviser, postpones sale.

text.p: Poland's largest insurer Powszechny Zaklad Ubezpieczen (PZU) said on Wednesday it had chosen an adviser to carry out its privatisation but that its sale to selected investors would be put off to April from March.

PZU's deputy president Ryszard Micyk said his firm had chosen a foreign investment bank, which he did not name, to negotiate with institutional investors taking up to 50 percent of fully state-owned PZU's shares.
"The adviser has already been chosen, but we have not signed an agreement yet, so I can not disclose its name at the moment, but I can tell you it's a well-known investment bank," Micyk told Reuters.

He said the company, which had earlier planned a March sale, was likely to find investors and sell the shares by the end of April. PZU's bourse debut was likely to take place in February next year, he added.
He said the sale was postponed due to longer than expected preparations of PZU financial standing assessment and information memorandum, which would be presented to the prospective investors.
"We hope the first stage (of the privatisation) would be concluded by the end of April...and as far as entering the bourse is concerned, February next year is the earliest date," he said.

The company plans a new share issue of 250-750 million zlotys for selected institutional investors, domestic and foreign. Under the plan, each of the investors will have no more than 10-15 percent of the shares.

Micyk said PZU was interested in attracting investors such as European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), the International Finance Corporation (IFC), Polish leading banks and others, but said no negotiations had been carried yet.
According to unaudited results, PZU had a net loss of 90 million zlotys on 3.5-billion-zloty gross premiums last year. Micyk said the company should show profit this year.
Micyk also said it was introducing modern Audatex and Eurotax systems for assessing car damages and repair costs, which would let it reduce its costs.
